description: Adjustable LDO set to 5.21V for the DAC AVDD
notes: Off protected +12V. ~13mA load incl. the divider, ~90mW. Decouples DAC full scale from the rack's +-5% +5V rail. TOLERANCE IS A BENCH TASK, NOT A SPEC TASK: worst case spans 0.66V against a ~0.55V window and no nominal value fits on paper, but this is one unit with a TO-92 part, two through-hole resistors and a voltmeter. E7 measures where the DAC's top codes start compressing against AVDD and selects R2 from that - BUT NOT BELOW 5.00V: the DAC8568's C grade is specified only for AVDD 5.0-5.5V (SBAS430E), which this row and the E7 step did not know. | 2026-09-21, from TI SLCS144E now in the repo (datasheets/discrete-and-power/LM317LZ.pdf): TI's LM317L needs 'Minimum output current to maintain regulation: 1.5 typ / 2.5 MAX mA', and Recommended Operating Conditions give Io 2.5-100mA. NOT the full LM317's 10mA. *** BUT THIS ROW SAYS MANUFACTURER 'multiple' AND THAT IS NOW DANGEROUS: *** ST's and ON's LM317L are different documents with different minimum-load numbers (commonly 3.5mA), and the classic Z suffix is an ST/ON TO-92 marking rather than a TI orderable - TI's document covers the LP package. A bleeder sized for TI's 2.5mA UNDER-LOADS a 3.5mA part. Either name the manufacturer or size for the worst case across candidates. The ~13mA load clears every reading, so nothing is broken today; the hazard is a future reader trimming the divider current. Reference 1.20/1.25/1.30V confirms the +-4% claim; line regulation 0.01%/V typ, 0.02%/V max at 25degC; output noise 30uV PER VOLT of output over 10Hz-10kHz, so ~150uV RMS at 5.21V; ripple rejection 65dB typ, rising to 66 min / 80 typ WITH a 10uF cap on ADJUSTMENT - which C-REG-ADJ already fits

Vout = 1.25*(1+475/150) = 5.21V. WAS 240R/768R at 1%, whose stated '+-4% = 5.04-5.46V' ignored both the divider tolerance and I_ADJ. Smaller R2 halves the I_ADJ term to 24-48mV; 0.1% parts cost pennies in the same order. The LM317's own 1.20-1.30V reference is the dominant term and no divider fixes it - so R2 is SELECTED ON THE BENCH at E7 (this is a population of one), and the value here is the starting point. Buy a handful of neighbouring E96 values

description: LM317 ADJ bypass and output cap
notes: ADJ bypass drops output noise to ~50uV RMS. Output cap for LDO stability. 2026-09-21: TI SLCS144E confirms the mechanism and the size - ripple rejection goes from 65dB typ to 66 min / 80 typ WITH a 10uF capacitor from ADJUSTMENT to ground, which is what this row already specifies

One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Rated >=1A - the common 0805 600R part is ~300mA and a saturated bead is a wire. The '470uF at the load' half of this row moved out: entry bulk is C-BULK-RAIL, strip bulk is C-STRIP-BULK, and this row was double-booking them | *** 2026-09-21 PART CHOSEN, AND THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE DATASHEET THAT CHOSE IT. *** Laird MI1206K601R-10, drawing rev E 08/05/13, banked at datasheets/discrete-and-power/MI1206K601R-10-ferrite-bead.pdf. Chosen on ONE criterion: it is the only >=1A 600R 1206 part found whose datasheet actually PUBLISHES AN IMPEDANCE-UNDER-DC-BIAS CURVE, with traces at 0 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 1500 mA. Verified by rendering the sheet and reading it by hand - the file is vector CAD. Specs off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** THE '>=1A' RULE DOES NOT DO WHAT THIS ROW SAYS IT DOES. *** The row's reason is 'a saturated bead is a wire' - but a bead's CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it tells you nothing about saturation. Read off this part's own bias curve at 100 MHz: 0 A ~614 ohm, 250 mA ~431, 500 mA ~157, 1000 mA ~72, 1500 mA (its RATED current) ~51. To prove the point a 3000 mA part in the same package with the same 600 ohm nominal was banked alongside it (HI1206N601R-10-ferrite-bead.pdf): at 500 mA it reads ~145 ohm, i.e. SLIGHTLY WORSE than the 1.5 A part. Doubling the rating buys nothing but 0.02 ohm of DCR. *** WHAT THIS MEANS PER BRANCH: *** FB4 (+5V, mA), FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part of the curve and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. FB2 carries the umbilical at the 359 mA of figures.yaml `umbilical-current` and gets ~280-310 ohm - ROUGHLY HALF THE 600 OHM THIS ROW NAMES - falling to ~245-275 ohm at the 392 mA module total. No 1206 600R bead of any rating fixes FB2; the bias curve shifts the impedance peak UP IN FREQUENCY, so the bead does not die, its useful band simply slides off 100 MHz. EITHER the requirement for FB2 is restated at its real operating current, or FB2 becomes a physically larger part. IR DROP at 0.080 ohm max: 28.7 mV at 359 mA (10.3 mW), 31.4 mV at 392 mA, 3.6 mV at 45 mA. SECOND SOURCE: Murata BLM31PG601SN1L is an electrical twin and far better stocked, but MURATA'S PDF CARRIES NO DC-BIAS CURVE EITHER - that data lives only in SimSurfing - so it can be an alternate flagged 'bias assumed, not documented', never the characterised part. The earlier researcher's refusal to bank a Wurth WE-CBF for exactly this reason was right and is upheld

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: NOT 47uF on every rail. The +12V branch carries the LM317's divider, the DAC and the comparator, about 22mA against -12V's 10mA - so at 47uF each it collapses 2.2x faster and every rack power-down leaves the op-amps with V+ near 0 and V- at -6 to -8V for ~30ms, pulling all six jacks toward the surviving negative rail. 100uF on +12V balances the decay. 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004; NOT the strip capacitance, which belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK
